Parte afilada que aloja o óstio interno: Tapered part that lodges the internal urethral orifice.
Parte posterior e convexa da bexiga, sen: Posterior and convex part of the bladder, opposite the apex.
Localiza-se entre o ápice e o fundo e é: Located between the apex and the fundus, it is the largest part of the bladder.
Tem relação com a sínfise púbica em ambo: It is related to the pubic symphysis in both sexes.
Músculo liso que compõe a parede da bexi: The detrusor muscle, a smooth muscle forming the wall of the urinary bladder; its contraction promotes bladder emptying.
Área triangular limitada pelos óstios do: Triangular area bounded by the ureteric orifices and the internal urethral orifice. Its mucosa is smooth, differentiating it from the rest of the bladder.
Passa posteriormente à veia cava inferio: Passes posterior to the inferior vena cava and is longer than the left.
Tubo muscular (25 a 30 cm de comprimento: Muscular tube (25 to 30 cm long) that transports urine from the kidneys to the urinary bladder. It is divided into abdominal, pelvic, and intramural parts.
Passa anteriormente à parte abdominal da: Passes anterior to the abdominal part of the aorta and is longer than the right. It receives the left suprarenal vein and the left gonadal vein.
Os rins são dois órgãos localizados na r: The kidneys are two organs located in the posterior region of the abdomen, on each side of the vertebral column. They are retroperitoneal, with the right kidney being slightly lower than the left, due to its relationship with the liver.
As glândulas suprarrenais estão associad: The suprarenal glands are associated with the superior pole of each kidney.
Artérias renais extra hilares são ramos: Extra-hilar renal arteries are accessory renal arteries, most commonly arising from the abdominal aorta, that enter the kidney outside the hilum, often at the superior or inferior poles. They represent important anatomical variations in renal surgery and transplantation.
Consiste em uma fenda na margem medial d: The renal hilum is a vertical slit on the medial border of the kidney through which the renal vessels, nerves, lymphatics, and ureter pass.
Tem múltiplas ramificações intraparenqui: The renal artery divides into segmental arteries, which give rise to interlobar, arcuate, and interlobular arteries within the kidney.
Espaço no interior dos rins ocupado pela: Space within the kidneys occupied by the renal pelvis, calyces, vessels, nerves, and a variable amount of fat.
Recebe urina da papila renal e conduz at: The minor calyx receives urine from the renal papilla and drains it into a major renal calyx.
É a extremidade superior dilatada do ure: It is the dilated upper end of the ureter. It receives two or three major renal calyces.
Cada rim tem dois ou três cálices maiore: Each kidney has two or three major calyces. Each major calyx receives two or three minor calyces.
Faixa contínua de tecido pálido externo: The renal cortex forms a continuous outer layer of pale tissue surrounding the renal medulla.
Extensões do córtex renal que se projeta: Extensions of the renal cortex that project into the medulla, situated between the renal pyramids.
São saliências formadas pelos vértices d: These are prominences formed by the apices of the medullary pyramids. They open into the minor renal calyces.
A medula renal é composta pelo conjunto: The renal medulla is composed of renal pyramids, the number of which varies from about 8 to 18 in each kidney.
Membrana transparente e fibrosa que prot: Transparent and fibrous membrane that externally protects the kidney.
É uma condensação de tecido conjuntivo q: It is a condensation of connective tissue that surrounds the kidney, situated between two adipose layers: the pararenal fat external to it and the perirenal fat more internal (between the renal fascia and the fibrous capsule).
Conduz a urina da bexiga (óstio interno: Conducts urine from the bladder (internal urethral orifice) to the external environment (external urethral orifice). In women, it is short, about three to five centimeters, which facilitates the occurrence of urinary tract infections.
Atravessa o bulbo e o corpo esponjoso do: Passes through the bulb and corpus spongiosum of the penis. It is about 15cm long and ends at the external urethral orifice, which opens at the glans penis.
Atravessa o assoalho da pelve e possui c: The membranous urethra passes through the pelvic floor and is approximately 1 cm long.
A uretra masculina é uma estrutura comum: The male urethra is a structure common to the urinary and genital systems. It begins at the internal urethral orifice and measures approximately 20 cm in length. The prostatic urethra is about 3 cm long and is surrounded by the prostate.
